Build paired-jackknife (JK2) replicate weights for TIMSS and PIRLS

Source: R/jk2_weights.R
jk2_weights.Rd

The IEA studies (TIMSS, PIRLS, ICCS, ICILS) do not ship replicate weights. They ship the final weight together with a jackknife zone (JKZONE) and a within-zone replicate indicator (JKREP, coded 0 or 1). jk2_weights() builds one replicate weight per zone from these three columns, so that the data can be passed to any estimator with rep_method = "JK2".

Usage

jk2_weights(
  data,
  weight = "TOTWGT",
  zone = "JKZONE",
  rep = "JKREP",
  prefix = "JKW"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of student-level records.

weight

Name of the final weight column (default "TOTWGT").

zone

Name of the jackknife zone column (default "JKZONE").

rep

Name of the within-zone replicate indicator, coded 0 or 1 (default "JKREP").

prefix

Prefix of the new columns (default "JKW"), which are named prefix1, prefix2, ... in the order of the sorted zone values.

Value

data with one added replicate-weight column per zone. The names of the new columns are stored in the attribute "repweights".

Details

For the replicate of zone \(h\), the weight of every student in that zone is multiplied by \(2 \times\) JKREP: one half of the zone gets twice its weight and the other half gets zero. Students in all other zones keep their weight. With these weights the sampling variance is \(\sum_h (\hat\theta_h - \hat\theta)^2\), which is the "JK2" factor of rep_factor().

This is the construction with one replicate per zone (75 replicates for 75 zones). From TIMSS 2015 and PIRLS 2016 on, the IEA reports use two replicates per zone and halve the sum. Both are estimators of the same sampling variance, but they do not give identical numbers, so standard errors from these weights can differ slightly from the published ones for those cycles.

References

Foy, P. & LaRoche, S. (2020). Estimating standard errors in the TIMSS 2019 results. In M. O. Martin, M. von Davier & I. V. S. Mullis (Eds.), Methods and Procedures: TIMSS 2019 Technical Report. TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center.

Examples

# a toy sample: 4 zones, 2 schools per zone, 3 students per school
d <- data.frame(
  JKZONE = rep(1:4, each = 6),
  JKREP  = rep(rep(0:1, each = 3), times = 4),
  TOTWGT = 1,
  score  = c(480, 510, 495, 530, 500, 520, 470, 505, 490, 515, 525, 500,
             540, 495, 510, 485, 500, 530, 505, 515, 490, 520, 480, 510)
)
d <- jk2_weights(d)
reps <- attr(d, "repweights")
lsa_model(d, ~ 1, "score", weight = "TOTWGT", repweights = reps,
          rep_method = "JK2")
#> Model: stats::lm(<PV> ~ 1)
#>   1 plausible value(s)  |  n = 24
#>   Variance: JK2, 4 replicate weights (+ PV imputation); t reference
#> 
#> 
#>             Estimate Std.Error     t  df p
#> (Intercept)      505      4.32 116.9 Inf 0
#> 
#> fitter = stats::lm
